content:
This year can be said to be the first year of super apps. OpenAI recently launched its own super app and admitted that the App is "a bit of a mess." Meanwhile, Microsoft's CEO also confirmed that a Copilot super app will be launched in the near future.

The Microsoft Copilot "super app" will integrate Cowork, chat, and coding features into one.

Microsoft is developing an AI "super app" that integrates Copilot's chat, coding, and agent capabilities. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said at Wednesday's earnings call that the app will launch this year, covering "consumer and business experiences." Nadella stated: "Copilot is rapidly evolving from chat to Cowork, and further toward Autopilot. This quarter, we are integrating these Copilot experiences—including coding capabilities—into one super app... This is a major step, and I look forward to sharing more details with you later."

OpenAI's process of launching its own "super app" can be described as a mess, but this clearly has not deterred other companies from continuing down the super app path.

Perhaps Microsoft will be able to more successfully deliver a multifunctional all-in-one app and avoid repeating OpenAI's mistakes.

That said, CEO Satya Nadella also recently stated that the company is gradually transforming from apps and focusing on agents. The AI era is still in its early stages, and the trends and best practices surrounding AI-centric interfaces are still changing rapidly.

As for Apple, there is no sign of a shift toward a super app strategy; on the contrary, the company continues to launch new and specialized standalone apps. Whether it will change direction in the future remains to be seen.

What are your thoughts on the recent "super app" craze? Feel free to share with us in the comment section.
